text:
B: Alright. Can you hear me?
A: Yeah.
B: Sound. I'm Darren.
A: Gemma.
B: Gemma. That's funny, that's my partner's name.
A: Right.
B: And the last girl I had said she'd just spoken to a Gemma who was a student nurse. Was that you?
A: Kayleigh? Yeah, that was me. First one.
B: Small world, innit. Well. Small study.
A: Suppose.
B: Erm, so where are you, then?
A: Catford. South-east London.
B: I'm Sutton-in-Ashfield. North Notts.
A: Never heard of it, sorry.
B: No, people haven't. Old mining towns. My grandad was down the pit. There's a drawing of a headstock behind me, if you can see it.
A: Oh, yeah. You do that?
B: Yeah. Years ago.
A: I'm not really into art, to be honest. It's nice though.
B: Fair enough. Not everyone's thing.
A: What's your job?
B: Warehouse. Picking and loading, off the M1. Fifty-odd hours a week. You're on a ward, she said?
A: Acute medical. Final year. It's long days and nights, I'm basically full-time without the pay.
B: Gemma, my Gemma, she's a carer. Bad back off the lifting. Is that, erm, is that a normal thing, or should she be getting it looked at? Sorry, you're not at work.
A: No, it's fine. It's really common. If it's going down her leg or she's getting numbness, she wants to see her GP. Otherwise physio, if she can get a referral. And proper hoist use, which never happens, I know.
B: Never. That's what she says. There's never two of them free.
A: Yeah. It's the same on the ward. Half the HCAs I worked with had bad backs by thirty.
B: Right. Cheers, that's useful, honestly. I'll tell her. She won't listen, but I'll tell her.
A: They never do. My husband's a gas engineer, he's the same with his knees.
B: Do you get time to do anything, with nights and that?
A: Netball on a Tuesday, when the rota lets me. Which it hasn't for three weeks. You?
B: Bike, mostly. Old railway lines round us, they've made them into trails. And the dog. Mabel. She's old, so it's more of a shuffle than a walk now.
A: Dean wants a dog. I keep saying no.
B: Get an old one. They just sleep. Mabel does about twenty hours a day.
A: That's actually the best argument I've heard. Don't tell him.
B: Ha, I won't. What's he cook you, then, if he's—
